answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Home to the only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World: the Great Pyramid of Giza.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Africa's most populous country, with over 200 million people.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: Named after Mount Kenya, Africa's second-highest peak.

answers.name: Morocco
answers.fact: Fez has what's often called the world's oldest operating university.

answers.name: Ethiopia
answers.fact: Runs on its own calendar, roughly seven to eight years behind the Gregorian one.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: The first sub-Saharan colony to win independence, in 1957.

answers.name: Madagascar
answers.fact: Around 90% of its wildlife lives nowhere else on Earth.

answers.name: Djibouti
answers.fact: Hosts military bases for the US, China, France and Japan.

answers.name: Burkina Faso
answers.fact: The name means 'land of upright people'.

answers.name: Tanzania
answers.fact: Home to Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain.

answers.name: Uganda
answers.fact: Home to about half the world's mountain gorillas.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Hyperinflation in 2008 produced a 100-trillion-dollar banknote.

answers.name: Zambia
answers.fact: Shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe.

answers.name: Algeria
answers.fact: Africa's largest country by area.

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: Over 90% desert.

answers.name: Tunisia
answers.fact: Star Wars' Tatooine is named after the Tunisian town of Tataouine.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Has more ancient pyramids than Egypt.

answers.name: South Sudan
answers.fact: The world's newest widely recognised country, independent since 2011.

answers.name: Somalia
answers.fact: Has the longest coastline in mainland Africa.

answers.name: Senegal
answers.fact: Its capital, Dakar, was the finish line of the famous Paris–Dakar Rally.

answers.name: Cameroon
answers.fact: Nicknamed 'Africa in miniature' for its varied landscapes.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Africa's second-largest country, holding most of the Congo rainforest.

answers.name: Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Its capital, Brazzaville, faces Kinshasa straight across the Congo River.

answers.name: Angola
answers.fact: Portuguese-speaking, and independent since 1975.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: Its flag features an AK-47 rifle.

answers.name: Namibia
answers.fact: Sossusvlei has some of the tallest sand dunes in the world.

answers.name: Botswana
answers.fact: Home to the world's largest elephant population.

answers.name: Rwanda
answers.fact: Has the highest share of women in parliament of any country.

answers.name: Mali
answers.fact: Home to Timbuktu, once a great centre of Islamic scholarship.

answers.name: Niger
answers.fact: Named after the Niger River, which only crosses its south-west corner.

answers.name: Chad
answers.fact: Lake Chad has shrunk by around 90% since the 1960s.

answers.name: Côte d'Ivoire
answers.fact: The world's biggest cocoa producer.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: Its capital, Freetown, was founded as a home for freed slaves.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: Africa's oldest republic, independent since 1847.

answers.name: The Gambia
answers.fact: Mainland Africa's smallest country: a thin strip along the Gambia River.

answers.name: Malawi
answers.fact: Lake Malawi covers about a fifth of the country.

answers.name: Mauritius
answers.fact: The dodo's only home, until it was wiped out in the 1600s.

answers.name: Seychelles
answers.fact: Africa's smallest country by population.

answers.name: Eritrea
answers.fact: Its capital, Asmara, is UNESCO-listed for its modernist Italian buildings.

answers.name: Lesotho
answers.fact: Entirely surrounded by South Africa, and its lowest point is still about 1,400 m up.

answers.name: Gabon
answers.fact: Around 85% covered in rainforest.

answers.name: Guinea
answers.fact: The Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise in its highlands.

answers.name: Benin
answers.fact: Birthplace of the Vodun religion.

answers.name: Togo
answers.fact: Long and thin: under 120 km wide.

answers.name: Burundi
answers.fact: Its royal drummers' ritual dance is UNESCO-listed.

answers.name: Central African Republic
answers.fact: The name says it: it sits near the middle of the continent.

answers.name: Mauritania
answers.fact: Formally abolished slavery in 1981, the last country to do so.

answers.name: Cabo Verde
answers.fact: Singer Cesária Évora, the 'Barefoot Diva', came from these islands.

answers.name: Comoros
answers.fact: A major source of ylang-ylang, a key perfume ingredient.

answers.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
answers.fact: Africa's second-smallest country by area.

answers.name: Equatorial Guinea
answers.fact: The only African country with Spanish as an official language.

answers.name: Guinea-Bissau
answers.fact: One of the world's biggest cashew producers.

answers.name: Eswatini
answers.fact: Called Swaziland until 2018, and one of the world's last absolute monarchies.
